rv.q: But it is that heightened exaltation that makes Williams’s work glorious, and it is woefully missing in this cautious, bloodless production.
Curiously, I had the same reaction this time around.
But this revival, like the play’s previous incarnations, mainly proves that Orpheus Descending never really works.

From its heavy-handed poetry to its confused metaphors, the problems that plagued Orpheus Descending back in 1957 (and its earlier incarnation as Battle of Angels ) remain on display in this new production.
That is more or less my reaction to Theatre for a New Audience’s revival of “Orpheus Descending,” Tennessee Williams’ rarely-produced 1957 play – hard-working, but just too peculiar.
The current revival, though, is one I’d caution any such director not to look back on.
In the end, this is a flawed production of a flawed play.

cn.t: Critics find this revival of Williams' notoriously problematic 1957 drama fails to ignite, with the overheated Southern Gothic melodrama and doomed lovers story lacking the heat and conviction needed to overcome the play's inherent flaws.
